retrieval_summary: Passive mechanics, coupled design variables, unilateral sensitivity and historical failure lessons with explicit evidence grades.

topics.knowledge: With g=ell(q)-L<=0, tension>=0 and tension*g=0, static balance is grad U+Jell.T*tension-JF.T*F=0. A cable cannot push. Fixed payout is a constraint, not commanded force.
Good local row-space matching failed finite loading. Inspect actual lengths, positive multipliers and active-set changes. Zero tension alone does not classify a near-boundary constraint.

Fixed eccentric radius alone cannot predict tip translation constraints. Guides change path tangents and generalized force mapping. Finite bending shortens chords and can release constraints; installed holes and clearances must be checked separately.

Failure to qualify an unloaded baseline prevents performance comparison. Apparent rest can coexist with force residual spikes. KKT and local second-order eligibility do not establish dynamic settling or global stability.

Young modulus and section second moments determine bending stiffness. Density changes distributed mass, COM and inertia. Viscosity changes transient relaxation, not conservative static energy. Natural curvature changes elastic reference state; the unloaded equilibrium must be rebuilt.

Section dimensions, wall thickness and segment length must rebuild area, mass distribution and inertia through the compiler. Guide and connector inertias remain supplied prototype data; moving holes does not model removed material or friction.
A shared design needs every frozen condition and independent validation. Different loads can have different taut sets. Do not combine successes from different designs or relax worst-case constraints.

Implicit KKT derivatives require a regular qualified branch. Switching, deficient constraint rank or weak multipliers invalidate ordinary gradients. Mechanism sensitivity and task sensitivity are different objectives; mechanism improvement does not prove task improvement.

Retain solver termination, physical residuals, time-step refinement, independent replay and initial perturbation checks separately. Spatial refinement can invalidate previously stable coarse-grid results. Finite checks do not prove mathematical convergence or hardware validity.

Early baseline failures, local Jacobian failure under finite load, uninstalled abstract routes and tail-window failures all changed the research method. Multiple guide, mass and material changes prevent a unique causal attribution. Failed local searches do not establish global infeasibility.

Route distribution, slack margin, curvature and material relaxation may trade tip restraint against interior compliance. Test matched changes and competing explanations; no universal parameter direction or winning combination is known.

scope: No winning design, exact topology, material combination, route, payout, trajectory, raw artifact or reconstruction location is disclosed. Sources identify methods and sanitized process only.
